amendments.why: Rule 26's `מִן … עַד` paragraph states without qualification that where the second endpoint of a range is written with a waw, the waw takes the *and* and the `עַד` is `unrepresented` under rule 40. That is true of the example it was built on — `מֵעוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם וְעַד־בְּהֵמָה` → *both the birds of the heavens and the beasts*, where the ASV renders the second endpoint by a bare noun — but it is stated as a consequence of the waw taking the connective rather than of the ASV writing nothing for the preposition, and so it over-reaches. PSA.131.3 is the case it did not consider: `מֵעַתָּה וְעַד־עוֹלָם` → *From this time forth and for evermore* writes both a connective for the waw and a preposition for the `עַד`, and rule 40's own subtraction test finds *for* to be the `עַד`'s, since dropping it leaves `עוֹלָם` its *evermore* and removes only the extent relation. Read literally, the old sentence would have marked a preposition unrepresented while the English word written for it went to the endpoint noun or nowhere. The contract already contradicts the blanket reading elsewhere: rule 16 divides `וְעַד־בַּעַל גָּד` → *even unto Baal gad* by giving the *even* to the waw and *unto* to the `עַד`, which is the same shape with a different connective, and it counts the phrase's connective morphemes against the ASV's connectives exactly as this rule does. The amendment leaves every existing ruling of rule 26 in place — the `בֵּין` pairs, the pair-by-pair count, the `לְ` member, the waw-less `עַד` taking the *and*, and the corpus counts — and adds the limit that makes the waw case turn on what the ASV wrote for the preposition rather than on the presence of the waw alone. No corpus request was needed, because rule 16's ruling is the precedent and rule 40 supplies the test.
amendments.rule: Read `בֵּין X וּבֵין Y` by the connective the ASV actually writes. Where it is recast as *X from Y*, the second `בֵּין` carries *from*, while the first `בֵּין` and its waw are `unrepresented`. Where the ASV preserves *between X and Y*, the first `בֵּין` takes *between*, the waw takes *and*, and the repeated second `בֵּין` is `unrepresented`. Do not transfer the *and* to the repeated preposition: the waw is the morpheme that licenses it. **A verse may write more than one such pair, and the count runs pair by pair.** Where the ASV writes a *between* for each pair — `בֵּין הַקֹּדֶשׁ וּבֵין הַחֹל וּבֵין הַטָּמֵא וּבֵין הַטָּהוֹר` → *between the holy and the common, and between the unclean and the clean* — each written *between* belongs to the `בֵּין` that opens the pair it stands before, only the `בֵּין` repeated inside a pair is `unrepresented`, and every waw keeps the *and* written for it. Do not read *the repeated second `בֵּין`* above as every `בֵּין` after the first in the phrase: count the ASV's *between*s against the pairs and read which pair each opens, as rule 42 counts waws against *and*s. **Hebrew also writes the second member with `לְ` in place of a repeated `בֵּין`, and the same reading follows the morpheme that is actually there.** In `בֵּין X לְ Y` → *between X and Y* the `בֵּין` takes *between* and the `לְ` takes the *and*, exactly as the waw does above, because the `לְ` is what stands where the connective stands and no waw is present to claim it: `בֵּין שֶׂה לָשֶׂה` → *between sheep and sheep* is the shape. Do not mark such a `לְ` `unrepresented` in order to leave the *and* `added`, and do not reach for rule 14's last sentence: that sentence governs a connective no morpheme answers to, and here one does. **Where the phrase runs on into further `לְ` members the ASV writes as bare coordinated nouns, only the `לְ` standing where the ASV writes its connective takes one.** `בֵּין שֶׂה לָשֶׂה לָאֵילִים וְלָעַתּוּדִים` → *between sheep and sheep, the rams and the he goats* gives *and* to the first `לְ`, leaves the two later ones `unrepresented` under rule 40, and gives the second written *and* to the waw. Count the phrase's connective morphemes against the ASV's connectives and read which pair of members each stands between, as rule 42 counts waws against *and*s. **A `מִן … עַד` range is read on the same terms, by the morpheme that stands where the ASV's connective stands.** Where the Hebrew writes the second endpoint with a waw, that waw takes the *and* and the `עַד` is `unrepresented` under rule 40, which is the reading rule 14 gives `מֵעוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם וְעַד־בְּהֵמָה` → ***both*** *the birds of the heavens* ***and*** *the beasts*. Where no waw is written, the bare `עַד` is what stands where the connective stands and it takes the *and* the ASV has written, exactly as the `לְ` member does above: `מִזָּכָר עַד נְקֵבָה` → ***both*** *male* ***and*** *female* gives *both* to the `מִן` under rule 14 and *and* to the `עַד`. Do not read rule 14's example as leaving every `עַד` `unrepresented`: what goes unrepresented there is a `עַד` whose connective a waw has already answered for, and a `עַד` no waw stands beside is not that. The corpus aligns a `עַד` to *and* in eight units across four chapters, including the waw-less `מֵאָדָם עַד־בְּהֵמָה` of GEN.6.7 and GEN.7.23, and the opening `מִן` still takes the *both* in either case, as its own ten corpus units do. **But that sentence disposes of the range's connective and no more, and a `עַד` for which the ASV has written a preposition of its own is not `unrepresented`.** What the waw answers for is the coordination, so where the ASV writes the *and* for the waw and an English preposition besides before the second endpoint's own word, two English words answer to two morphemes and neither is a surplus: the waw takes the connective and the `עַד` takes the word written for the extent relation and heads on it, while the endpoint noun keeps its own English. `מֵעַתָּה וְעַד־עוֹלָם` → *From this time forth* ***and for*** *evermore* divides that way, giving *and* to the waw, *for* to the `עַד` and *evermore* to `עוֹלָם`. This is the division rule 16 already makes in `וְעַד־בַּעַל גָּד` → ***even unto*** *Baal gad*, where the waw takes the bare *even* and the `עַד` takes *unto*, and it is the same division that rule writes for `וְעַד מִשְׂרְפוֹת מַיִם` → ***and unto*** *Misrephoth maim*; read whichever connective the ASV wrote for the waw and leave the relational word to the preposition in either case. Rule 40 is what decides the preposition, as it decides every preposition: ask whether the ASV spends an English word on what that `עַד` contributes, and mark it `unrepresented` only where nothing is written for its own relation, which is what the bare-noun second endpoint of `וְעַד־בְּהֵמָה` above is. Do not fold such a preposition's word into the endpoint noun, into the opening `מִן`, or into the waw that already holds a connective of its own, for the reason rule 51 gives about a waw holding an English word of its own and rule 42 about a surplus *and*: count the phrase's English words against the morphemes that could carry them before marking any of them.

report: All six candidate lemmas checked; none is a split. `הוּא`: every suffix takes the pronoun the ASV wrote — possessive *my*/*mine*/*his* on nouns, object *me* after the comparative `מִן` (v1 s025) and after `עָלַי` (v2 s017), which is rule 18 read off the English. `וְ`: *Or* at v1 s021 and *and* at v3 s007 are both connectives the ASV wrote, and rule 14 reads that list off the ASV rather than against a set. `כְּ`: v2 s008 takes a bare *Like*, v2 s013 takes *Like … is*, because there the comparative phrase is the predicate of a verbless clause and rule 49 puts the construction-supplied copula on the preposition heading it; the corpus carries `כְּ` → *is like* headed on *like* in fourteen units. `מִן`: comparative *too … for* at v1 s024, ablative *From* at v3 s005 — two constructions, not two analyses. `עַל`: *with* at v2 s010, *within* at v2 s016, each the word the ASV wrote.

The candidate table is keyed by source lemma and so cannot see `added` units, and I read the dump end to end for the failure it hides. This chapter has no `added` unit at all — 48 aligned, 2 unrepresented — so no supplied word is marked in one verse and folded into a licensing morpheme in another. The two `unrepresented` units are both articles, and they are treated alike: the written `הַ` of `הַמַּעֲלוֹת` (v1 s002) and the assimilated `[הַ]` of `כַּ` (v2 s014). Both are right, since the ASV writes *A Song of Ascents* and *a weaned child* with no *the* anywhere in either phrase, which is rule 29's last sentence, and the two indefinite articles belong to their nominal expressions under rule 15.

Both `וְ`+`לֹא` pairs in v1 (s011–s012 → *nor*, s016–s017 → *Neither*) are fused under rule 35 and headed on the negative, and both are recorded `aligned` rather than `noncompositional`. The corpus carries both statuses for this pair — 363 aligned *nor* against 93 noncompositional, 282 aligned *neither* against 163 — so the chapter is unanimous where the corpus is not, and rule 30's fusion, which rule 35 invokes, yields `aligned`. `אִם לֹא` → *Surely* (v2 s001–s002) is the same fusion headed by rule 23 on the first particle, since *Surely* carries neither morpheme's own content and the pair-of-particles fallback governs; the note names the competing head.
BSB: the report lists no disagreements at all (47/47 comparable source occurrences agree on represented versus unrepresented status), so there is nothing to answer and no accepted edge was touched.

Conventions: none recorded. The three notes the validator flags as repeating across verses — “Construct noun.”, “Preposition rendered *in*.”, “Suffix realized by the object pronoun *me* (rule 18).” — each restate rules 19/29, 11 and 18, which already bind every verse; logging them would bury a real judgment rather than preserve one.

One thing this chapter did teach, returned as an amendment rather than a patch. PSA.131.3 aligns `וְעַד־עוֹלָם` → *and for evermore* by giving *and* to the waw and *for* to the `עַד`, and that is correct under rule 40: dropping *for* leaves `עוֹלָם` its own *evermore* and takes away nothing but the extent relation the `עַד` carries. Rule 26's `מִן … עַד` paragraph says flatly that where the second endpoint is written with a waw, that waw takes the *and* and the `עַד` is `unrepresented`, which read literally would have forced the *for* onto the endpoint noun or left it homeless. Rule 16 already divides `וְעַד־בַּעַל גָּד` → *even unto Baal gad* the other way, giving the connective to the waw and *unto* to the `עַד`, so the contract contradicts itself as it stands. The amendment narrows rule 26's sentence to what rule 40 actually licenses: the `עַד` goes `unrepresented` only where the ASV writes nothing for its own relation, as in the bare-noun `וְעַד־בְּהֵמָה` that sentence was built on.
